assessment: In this study, Guo et al. uncover a role for the transcription factor Klf9 in keeping adult hippocampal neural stem cells in a state of quiescence. Following relief from this molecular brake through Klf9 loss-of-function, neural stem cells undergo symmetric cell divisions that promote their self-renewal and expansion. This data suggest that Klf9 contributes to the molecular interplay that governs stem cell decisions between quiescence and activation on one hand and between distinct modes of cell divisions on the other.
